{{short description|British physicist}}
'''Ken Riley''' is a physicist.

==Career==
Ken Riley read mathematics at [[Clare College]], [[University of Cambridge]], and proceeded to a Ph.D. there in theoretical and experimental nuclear physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Fellows: Ken Riley |url=https://www.clare.cam.ac.uk/about/people/master-and-fellowship/emeritus-fellows/ken-riley |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603091020/https://www.clare.cam.ac.uk/about/people/master-and-fellowship/emeritus-fellows/ken-riley |archive-date=3 June 2025 |access-date=17 February 2026 |website=[[Clare College, Cambridge|Clare College, University of Cambridge]]}}</ref>

He became a research associate in elementary particle physics in [[Brookhaven National Laboratory|Brookhaven]], and then, having taken up lectureship at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], Cambridge, continued this research at the [[Rutherford Laboratory]] and [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford]]; in particular he was involved in the experimental discovery of a number of the early [[baryonic]] resonances.

He taught physics and mathematics for over 40 years at Clare College and served on many committees concerned with the teaching and examining of these subjects at all levels of tertiary and undergraduate education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Essential Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences |url=https://booksplea.se/essential-mathematical-methods-for-the-physical-sciences-by-k-f-riley/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260217164544/https://booksplea.se/essential-mathematical-methods-for-the-physical-sciences-by-k-f-riley/ |archive-date=17 February 2026 |access-date=17 February 2026 |website=Booksplease}}</ref> He was also a Senior Tutor and Admissions Tutor for twenty years.<ref name=":0" />

He is also one of the authors of ''200 Puzzling Physics Problems''<ref>{{Cite web |title=200 Puzzling Physics Problems - Peter Gnadig, Gyula Honyek, Ken Riley |url=http://www.iri.upc.edu/people/thomas/Collection/details/54047.html |access-date=2022-05-08 |website=www.iri.upc.edu}}</ref> and ''Mathematical Methods for Physics and Engineering''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematical Methods for Physics and Engineering |url=https://assets.cambridge.org/97805218/61533/frontmatter/9780521861533_frontmatter.pdf |access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref> He also wrote the memoir ''In Loco Parentis: a light-hearted look at the role of a Cambridge Tutor''.<ref name=":0" />
